edits.content:
-- Each Trends request is scaled to its own 0-100, so values only compare inside one request.
-- The ingester asks for one term per request (so each term uses the full range) and pulls
-- every request several times in one batch, because Trends samples. request_id is
-- <group>-<geo>-<year>-<batch>-<pull>. We keep the newest batch per (term group, geo,
-- study year) and take the per-day median across its pulls. Older multi-term requests
-- (the 2026-11 'day_off' group) are dropped: their terms shared one scale.
with source as (
    select
        *,
        cast(split_part(request_id, '-', 3) as integer) as study_year,
        split_part(request_id, '-', 4) as batch_id
    from {{ source('raw', 'trends_interest') }}
),

single_term_requests as (
    select request_id
    from source
    group by request_id
    having count(distinct term) = 1
),

newest_batch as (
    select source.term_group, source.geo, source.study_year, max(source.batch_id) as batch_id
    from source
    inner join single_term_requests using (request_id)
    group by source.term_group, source.geo, source.study_year
)

select
    source.term_group || '-' || source.geo || '-' || cast(source.study_year as varchar)
        || '-' || source.batch_id as request_id,
    source.study_year,
    source.term_group,
    source.geo,
    source.term,
    source.day as interest_date,
    median(cast(source.interest as double)) as interest,
    count(distinct source.request_id) as pull_count,
    bool_or(source.is_partial) as is_partial
from source
inner join single_term_requests using (request_id)
inner join newest_batch
    on source.term_group = newest_batch.term_group
    and source.geo = newest_batch.geo
    and source.study_year = newest_batch.study_year
    and source.batch_id = newest_batch.batch_id
group by
    source.term_group,
    source.geo,
    source.study_year,
    source.batch_id,
    source.term,
    source.day

-- Every signal as one daily value per (source, signal, geo, UTC day).
-- A value that could not be read is NULL with is_available = false: unavailable, never zero.
with trends as (
    select
        'google_trends' as source,
        'search:' || lower(term) as signal,
        case when term_group = 'hype' then 'hype' else 'day_off_intent' end as signal_family,
        geo,
        interest_date as signal_date,
        case when not is_partial then cast(interest as double) end as signal_value,
        not is_partial as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_trends__interest') }}
),

bluesky as (
    select
        'bluesky' as source,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'posts:day_off_gta' else 'posts:day_off' end as signal,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'day_off_gta' else 'day_off_intent' end as signal_family,
        'WORLD' as geo,
        hit_date as signal_date,
        case when bool_and(is_available) then cast(sum(hits_total) as double) end as signal_value,
        bool_and(is_available) as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_bluesky__daily_hits') }}
    group by gta_filter, hit_date
),

hacker_news as (
    select
        'hacker_news' as source,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'posts:day_off_gta' else 'posts:day_off' end as signal,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'day_off_gta' else 'day_off_intent' end as signal_family,
        'WORLD' as geo,
        hit_date as signal_date,
        case when bool_and(is_available) then cast(sum(hits_total) as double) end as signal_value,
        bool_and(is_available) as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_hn__daily_hits') }}
    group by gta_filter, hit_date
),

wikipedia as (
    select
        'wikipedia' as source,
        'pageviews:' || lower(article) as signal,
        case when article = 'Grand_Theft_Auto_VI' then 'hype' else 'reference' end as signal_family,
        'WORLD' as geo,
        view_date as signal_date,
        cast(views as double) as signal_value,
        true as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_wiki__pageviews') }}
)

select * from trends
union all
select * from bluesky
union all
select * from hacker_news
union all
select * from wikipedia

declarations.description: One row per Trends term per day: the per-day median over the pulls of the newest single-term batch for each (term group, geo, study year).

population.rule: Only single-term requests, newest batch per (term_group, geo, study_year). Multi-term requests are dropped because their terms shared one 0-100 scale (PTO squeezed call in sick to 3-8).

request_id.description: The batch the value came from (<group>-<geo>-<year>-<batch>); values only compare within one batch.

term_group.description: One group per term: call_in_sick, sick_day, day_off_work, or hype (GTA 6). Each requested on its own.

geo.description: 'US' for new batches; 'WORLD' only from older single-term hype pulls.

interest_date.description: The day Google reports, in Google's own day boundaries.

interest.description: Median relative search interest across the batch's pulls; 100 is the peak of a pull.

is_partial.description: True when any pull marked the day partial (Google's latest day while it fills in).

pull_count.description: How many pulls of the batch reported this day.

assumptions.decision: How to combine repeated Trends pulls
assumptions.chosen: per-day median across the pulls of the newest batch
assumptions.detail: user asked to fix Trends noise: Trends samples, so repeated pulls of the same request are medianed; pulls of one request share a scale
user approved one term per request; multi-term requests squeezed low-volume terms (call in sick 3-8)
user approved US-only, no PTO (HR-portal navigation, power take-off)

assumptions.chosen: third and fourth dash-separated parts of request_id
a day is partial when any pull marks it partial
assumptions.detail: conservative: a day still filling in for one pull is not settled

assumptions.chosen: the batch id <group>-<geo>-<year>-<batch>, one per median
assumptions.detail: a median spans the batch's pulls, so the row's provenance is the batch

declarations.description: One row per signal per day: every source's daily value in one shape.

population.rule: Every staged day of every source; Bluesky and Hacker News seeds are summed per day and filter.

source.description: google_trends, bluesky, reddit, hacker_news or wikipedia.

signal.description: What is counted, e.g. search:pto, posts:day_off, posts:day_off_gta, pageviews:grand_theft_auto_vi.

signal_family.description: day_off_intent (people saying or searching they are off), day_off_gta (the same, mentioning GTA), hype (interest in GTA itself), reference.

geo.description: US or WORLD. Only Google Trends has a US slice.

signal_date.description: UTC day (Google's own day for Trends).

signal_value.null_rule: NULL when the value could not be read: unavailable, never zero.
signal_value.description: Counts for posts and pageviews; relative 0-100 interest for Trends. Never add across signals or sources.

is_available.description: False when any part of the day's value failed to load or was partial.

assumptions.chosen: sum hits across seeds per day
assumptions.detail: a post matching two seeds counts twice; the double count is the same on both Thursdays, so the lift is unaffected in expectation
docs/methodology.md: missing is unavailable, never zero
Google flags the latest day isPartial while it fills in

assumptions.chosen: every Trends group except hype is day_off_intent
assumptions.detail: Trends day-off terms are now one group per term

assumptions.chosen: US call in sick, sick day, day off work; PTO and WORLD day-off signals removed
assumptions.detail: user approved the Trends fix: US only, no PTO
